title: What Is PDF/X-1a? How to Export a Print-Ready Book PDF | SparkPrep
h1: What is PDF/X-1a, and how do you export it for your book?
description: PDF/X-1a is the print standard many printers ask for. Learn what it means in plain English and how to export a PDF/X-1a file from InDesign, Affinity or Acrobat.
platforms: IngramSpark · Barnes & Noble Press · Lulu · Amazon KDP
lead: PDF/X-1a sounds like a code. It's just a strict kind of PDF that printers know will print the same every time.
errorNote: Paraphrased. Some printers require it; others strongly recommend it.
why:
A normal PDF can hold things that confuse a printing press: screen colors (RGB), fonts that aren't included, see-through effects that print unpredictably. PDF/X-1a is a set of rules that forbids those:

  • every font embedded,
  • colors in CMYK or spot colors only,
  • see-through effects flattened,
  • the trim and bleed size written into the file.

IngramSpark asks for PDF/X-1a, and following it solves most other file errors at the same time.

steps: Marks and Bleeds: tick Use Document Bleed Settings. Export.
Under PDF/X compliance, choose Convert to PDF/X-1a and run it.
Fix anything it can't convert, such as fonts that can't be embedded.
